title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page explore the relationship between the Production budgets and the worldwide revenues of the 104 films Figure 1.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt 

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Production budget (millions of US dollars)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Production budgets and worldwide revenues of the films.

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
This plot shows the relationship between the Runtime and the viewer’s ratings of the 104 films Figure 1
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating (0–10)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film runtimes and IMDb ratings.

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Release year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.title("James Bond film revenue over time")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()








The Bond films in this dataset run from 1995 to 2021.
